test_objectives.statement: abort(code, *args, **kwargs) must raise an Exception for every parametrized case, since each case body is wrapped in pytest.raises(Exception).
test_objectives.condition: for all five parametrized (scenario, has_app_context, code, args, kwargs) tuples

test_objectives.statement: When an app context is present (has_app_context True: 404, 500 with message, 418 with kwargs), the raised exception's string must contain f"Aborted with {code}".
test_objectives.condition: has_app_context is True and _cv_app.get(None) yields a non-None context

test_objectives.statement: When no app context is present (has_app_context False: 403, and 400 with positional and keyword arguments), the raised exception's string must contain f"Werkzeug abort {code}".
test_objectives.condition: has_app_context is False and _cv_app.get(None) returns None

scenario_hypotheses.description: The mocked context makes _cv_app.get(None) return the wired mock_ctx (mock_ctx.app = mock_app, mock_app.aborter = mock_aborter), so abort takes the true branch and invokes ctx.app.aborter(code, *args, **kwargs); the aborter raises the exception whose message contains 'Aborted with {code}'. Applies to the 404, 500-with-message and 418-with-kwargs parametrized cases.
scenario_hypotheses.condition: has_app_context is True and the context returned by _cv_app.get(None) is non-None

scenario_hypotheses.description: No app context is installed (or the patched _cv_app.get returns None), so abort skips the aborter branch and reaches the unconditional _wz_abort(code, *args, **kwargs), which raises the exception whose message contains 'Werkzeug abort {code}'. Applies to the 403 and 400-with-args/kwargs cases.
scenario_hypotheses.condition: has_app_context is False and _cv_app.get(None) evaluates to None

scenario_hypotheses.description: Alternative app-context path in which the context exists but ctx.app.aborter returns without raising; abort would then fall through to _wz_abort, so the exception reported by exc_info would originate from the Werkzeug abort call rather than from the aborter, which would conflict with the visible 'Aborted with {code}' assertion. Preserved as an alternative rather than a requirement.
scenario_hypotheses.condition: has_app_context is True and the mock aborter does not raise

dependency_constraints.statement: The context object's app attribute must expose a callable aborter; the test wires mock_ctx.app = mock_app and mock_app.aborter = mock_aborter before calling abort.
On the context branch abort forwards code plus all *args and **kwargs unchanged to ctx.app.aborter; the forwarded values are the parameterized code, args and kwargs of each case.

_wz_abort is the module-level name bound by 'from werkzeug.exceptions import abort as _wz_abort' and is what abort calls after the optional context branch; the test may therefore patch it to control the no-context exception.
The context lookup goes through the module-level context variable _cv_app imported from .globals, so a mock of that variable's get method (masked setup) is a plausible way to supply the context.
abort is annotated to return t.NoReturn and its docstring states it raises an HTTPException, so both paths are expected to terminate in a raised exception rather than a return value.

expected_interactions.statement: abort performs a single context lookup via _cv_app.get(None) at entry.
On the context path, ctx.app.aborter is invoked once with the case's code, *args and **kwargs (e.g. (404), (500, 'Internal Server Error'), (418, description="I'm a teapot")).
On the no-context path, _wz_abort is invoked once with the case's code, *args and **kwargs (e.g. (403), (400, 'Bad Request', description='Invalid input')).
On the context path _wz_abort is expected not to be reached, because the aborter call raises first and the call to _wz_abort follows it as an unconditional statement.
If the context-path aborter returned normally, _wz_abort would also be invoked with the same code, *args and **kwargs.
expected_interactions.condition: has_app_context is True and the aborter does not raise

verification_candidates.statement: Consider verifying that mock_aborter was called once with the parameterized code, *args and **kwargs on app-context cases (masked slot verify_002).
Consider verifying that the Werkzeug abort mock was called once with the parameterized code, *args and **kwargs on no-context cases (masked slot verify_004).
Consider verifying that the Werkzeug abort mock was not called on app-context cases (masked slot verify_003).
verification_candidates.condition: has_app_context is True and the aborter raises

verification_candidates.statement: The rationale/type expectation attached to the captured exception (masked slot verify_001) is not visible; only the two message substring assertions and the generic pytest.raises(Exception) wrapper can be read.

evidence.rationale: Shows the parametrization signature and the first app-context case (404, no args, no kwargs), establishing that has_app_context selects separate target paths.
Shows the no-context cases (403; 400 with an extra positional arg and a keyword arg) and a further app-context case with kwargs, fixing the concrete code/args/kwargs values to be forwarded.
Marks the branch in which the mock app/aborter wiring is installed, separating app-context scenarios from no-context ones.
Shows the visible object wiring: the context's app attribute exposes an aborter mock, which is the dependency the target function calls.

Marks an unconditional masked setup slot placed after the context wiring and before the abort call, consistent with patching the module-level werkzeug abort used on the no-context path; content is not visible.
Establishes the core test objective: abort is called with the parametrized code, *args and **kwargs and must raise an Exception, whose value is captured for later assertions.
Visible expected assertion for the app-context branch: the propagated exception message must contain 'Aborted with {code}'.
Visible expected assertion for the no-context branch: the propagated exception message must contain 'Werkzeug abort {code}'.
Confirms the message assertions are split by has_app_context, i.e. two mutually exclusive expected exception sources.
Target branch under test: the context lookup call and the conditional aborter invocation that forwards code, *args and **kwargs; also shows the aborter call is not returned or raised from explicitly.
Shows the unconditional fall-through call to the imported Werkzeug abort, reached only when the context branch does not raise.
Identifies the module-level name _wz_abort as werkzeug.exceptions.abort, the dependency invoked on the no-context path and the plausible patch target.
Shows _cv_app is a module-level import from flask.globals, i.e. the object whose get method supplies the context, matching the masked mocking of a context provider.

evidence.quote: def abort(code: int | BaseResponse, *args: t.Any, **kwargs: t.Any) -> t.NoReturn:
evidence.rationale: Signature shows the function accepts a status code (or response) plus arbitrary args/kwargs and is annotated NoReturn, supporting the expectation that every path raises rather than returns.

uncertainty.statement: The bodies of masked slots mock_stub_001..mock_stub_006 and verify_001..verify_004 are not visible, so the exact mocks created (context provider, aborter, werkzeug abort), their side effects, and any call assertions cannot be determined.

How the app context is simulated is undetermined: it could be a patch of flask.helpers._cv_app.get returning mock_ctx, or a real app context pushed onto the context stack; both would make the true branch feasible without appearing in the visible text.

Whether the app-context aborter mock raises or returns normally is not visible; if it returned normally, abort would continue into _wz_abort and the 'Aborted with {code}' assertion would need the Werkzeug path to produce that message.
The concrete exception types raised on either path are not determined by the visible text; only that they are subclasses of Exception and their message substrings are asserted.
